[Deprecation] Deprecate items scheduled for 0.29 (#55353)

Signed-off-by: yewentao256 <zhyanwentao@126.com>

affected_interfaces: vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py::AscendCommonAttentionMetadata (subclasses vLLM CommonAttentionMetadata; propagates removed _seq_lens_cpu/_num_computed_tokens_cpu in unpadded())
vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_scheduler.py::KVPoolScheduler and pool_worker.py::KVPoolWorker (read removed VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL env var)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This deprecation-cleanup commit removes several APIs that vllm-ascend depends on at runtime. The two critical breakages:

1) vLLM removed `CommonAttentionMetadata._seq_lens_cpu` and `_num_computed_tokens_cpu` fields plus the deprecated `seq_lens_cpu`/`num_computed_tokens_cpu` properties (vllm/v1/attention/backend.py), and `GPUModelRunner.build_common_attn_metadata` no longer populates them (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py). `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` (vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py) does NOT redeclare these fields, so any `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata(_seq_lens_cpu=...)` constructor call now raises TypeError and any `common_attn_metadata._seq_lens_cpu` read raises AttributeError. Migration: use the canonical `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` (still populated with `optimistic_seq_lens_cpu`) in place of `_seq_lens_cpu`; derive computed tokens as `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound - (query_start_loc_cpu[1:] - query_start_loc_cpu[:-1])`, mirroring the new upstream `deepseek_v4/compressor.py::_get_c128_boundary` and `mamba_attn.py`; use exact `seq_lens.cpu()` inside `vllm.utils.gpu_sync_debug.gpu_sync_allowed()` only when exactness is required. Note `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is only an optimistic upper bound during async spec-decode, so add the same async-spec-decode guard vLLM added (skip c128-boundary / raise on replayssm) wherever exact lengths are needed.

Files to fix (replace `_seq_lens_cpu`/`_num_computed_tokens_cpu` with `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound`/derived values):
- vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py::unpadded() (~291-292): drop `_seq_lens_cpu=`/`_num_computed_tokens_cpu=` propagation; keep subclass-owned `seq_lens_cpu`/`num_computed_tokens_cpu` fields.
- vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py (~3412): remove `_seq_lens_cpu=` kwarg (seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound already set); backends must fall back to `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` or `seq_lens.cpu()` when `seq_lens_cpu` is None in async mode.
- vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py (~318), mla_v1.py (~479-488), dsa_v1.py (~832-837,1307-1310), sfa_v1.py (~338-343), indexer_kpool.py (~191-196), context_parallel/dsa_cp.py (~362-370,483-486), mla_cp.py, worker/v2/attn_utils.py, worker/dcp_utils.py, worker/v2/model_runner.py: replace `_seq_lens_cpu` reads.
- vllm_ascend/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py (~727-729,1007-1027,2211-2214,2309-2324), step3p5.py (~423-427), dspark_proposer.py (~317-322), dflash_proposer.py (~223-224), spec_decode/utils.py, worker/v2/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py, aclgraph.py: stop passing/reading the removed fields and delete the now-obsolete CPU-shadow invalidation code (upstream removed it since there is no CPU shadow to invalidate).

2) vLLM removed the `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` env var (vllm/envs.py); `CacheConfig.prefix_cache_retention_interval` now defaults to 0. vllm-ascend reads the var via `getattr(envs, "VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL", None)`, which will silently return None and disable the DSv4 prefix-cache retention feature. Migrate vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py (~110), vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_scheduler.py (~109) and pool_worker.py (~662) to read `vllm_config.cache_config.prefix_cache_retention_interval`, or define a dedicated `VLLM_ASCEND_*` env var per vllm-ascend/AGENTS.md. Update docs (docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash.md, DeepSeek-V4-Pro.md, locale .po files) and e2e/nightly config YAMLs that export the removed var.

3) Tests: update tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py, tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kv_cache.py, tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_attn_builder.py, tests/ut/worker/test_dcp_manager.py, tests/ut/spec_decode/test_eagle_proposer.py, tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/attention_utils.py that pass `_seq_lens_cpu`/`_num_computed_tokens_cpu`/`seq_lens_cpu=` kwargs to CommonAttentionMetadata constructors.

Not applicable to Ascend: `AttentionConfig.use_fp4_indexer_cache` removal (not referenced), `VLLM_MM_HASHER_ALGORITHM` removal (not referenced), ROCm CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES deprecation (ROCm-specific), and the upstream mamba_attn/cross_attention/rocm_aiter changes (no Ascend equivalents).
deep_analysis.risk: HIGH. Without adaptation: (a) `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` construction raises TypeError and every `_seq_lens_cpu`/`_num_computed_tokens_cpu` access raises AttributeError, crashing all Ascend attention backends (attention/MLA/SFA/DSA/indexer), v1/v2 model runners, DCP/PCP paths, and spec-decode proposers (Eagle/DFlash/DSpark/Step3p5/MTP). (b) `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is an optimistic upper bound in async spec-decode; treating it as exact can corrupt block tables, context-lens, and chunked-prefill boundaries (the exact reason upstream guards the compressor c128-boundary and replayssm paths with an async guard). (c) The retention-interval config silently degrades to the new default (0) for DSv4 hybrid prefix caching / Mooncake-AscendStore offloading, and the `unpadded()` helper shared by eagle/step3p5/DCP/encoder paths could silently slice broken metadata. Requires e2e validation on NPU (MLA/SFA/DSA/spec-decode and DeepSeek-V4 prefix-cache scenarios).

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This commit changes the constructor signatures of YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding, DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding and MRotaryEmbedding (removing `extrapolation_factor`, `attn_factor`, `apply_yarn_scaling`; adding `mscale`, `mscale_all_dim`, `attention_factor`), changes the `get_rope()` extra-kwargs filter, deletes telechat3_scaling_rope.py, and stops re-scaling max_model_len for YaRN variants. vllm-ascend registers OOT replacements for these classes via CustomOp.register_oot (vllm_ascend/utils.py:766-774), so `get_rope()` instantiates the Ascend classes with the NEW kwargs.

1. CRITICAL - vllm_ascend/ops/rotary_embedding.py::AscendYaRNRotaryEmbedding.__init__ (line 281): replace kwargs `extrapolation_factor`/`attn_factor`/`apply_yarn_scaling` with `mscale: float | None = None`, `mscale_all_dim: float | None = None`, `attention_factor: float | None = None` (keep `beta_fast`/`beta_slow`/`truncate`), and compute `self.mscale` exactly like the new parent: `float(attention_factor)` if set, else `yarn_get_mscale(scaling_factor, mscale) / yarn_get_mscale(scaling_factor, mscale_all_dim)` if both set, else `yarn_get_mscale(scaling_factor)`. Forward these to `super().__init__`. Without this, ANY YaRN rope model on Ascend (e.g. GLM-4 yarn) raises TypeError at model init.
2. vllm_ascend/ops/rotary_embedding.py::AscendDeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding.__init__ (line 335): the class reimplements init and `_set_cos_sin_cache`, bypassing the parent, so it does not crash (it already accepts mscale/mscale_all_dim and get_rope no longer passes the removed args). Align numerics with the new parent: drop `extrapolation_factor` from `inv_freq_mask` in `_set_cos_sin_cache` (parent now always uses 1.0) and drop `* attn_factor` from `self.mscale`; consider removing the now-dead `extrapolation_factor`/`attn_factor` params.
3. AscendMRotaryEmbedding (line 509) inherits the new parent init and is construction-safe; verify cos/sin mscale output for M-RoPE+YaRN models since mscale semantics changed (attention_factor precedence).
4. tests/ut/ops/test_rotary_embedding.py: after updating AscendYaRNRotaryEmbedding, the `check_parent_init_signature_has_not_changed` assertions (lines 341-349) must pass again; `make_yarn_embedding` fixture uses only positional args and needs no change.
5. Verify (no code change expected): `_get_and_verify_max_len` (vllm/config/model.py) no longer re-scales max_model_len for rope_type yarn/deepseek_yarn/deepseek_llama_scaling, and `patch_legacy_rope_type` remaps telechat3-yarn -> yarn. vllm-ascend has no patch on these and inherits the behavior; run evals on YaRN/DeepSeek/Kimi-K3/GLM models to confirm max_model_len and KV cache sizing remain correct. telechat3 removal has no Ascend impact (no references).

affected_interfaces: CompilationConfig.resolve_cudagraph_mode_and_sizes (vllm/config/compilation.py) - new `piecewise_capture_available=True` kwarg plus new fallback logic that downgrades PIECEWISE/FULL_AND_PIECEWISE when piecewise capture is unavailable. Called directly by vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py:5814 and vllm_ascend/_310p/worker/v2/model_runner.py:486 (both still work via the default, but the fallback semantics are new).

VllmConfig._normalize_piecewise_cudagraph_mode / __post_init__ (vllm/config/vllm.py) - replaces the old 'override piecewise to NONE' logic; now maps FULL_AND_PIECEWISE to FULL_DECODE_ONLY (instead of NONE) for non-VLLM_COMPILE configs, and the normalization is also invoked AFTER current_platform.check_and_update_config. Ascend's check_and_update_config (vllm_ascend/platform.py:1187-1219) reacts to the resulting mode.

GPUModelRunner.compile_or_warm_up_model (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py) - inherited unchanged by ascend's MRV2 NPUModelRunner (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py:79). Now computes piecewise_capture_available = (VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH or has_compiled_submodule(model)); on ascend this is typically False, so piecewise modes are downgraded at warmup.
CUDAGraphMode.without_piecewise() (vllm/config/compilation.py) - new enum helper (PIECEWISE->NONE, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE->FULL_DECODE_ONLY) driving the new fallbacks.
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
No breaking signature changes (new kwarg is optional with default True; new methods are additive), so vllm-ascend compiles unchanged, but two behavioral changes need verification/adaptation on NPU:

1. MRV2 piecewise downgrade (highest attention): In vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py, NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner) inherits upstream compile_or_warm_up_model. After this commit it computes piecewise_capture_available = bool(envs.VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH or has_compiled_submodule(self.model)). Ascend sets VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 by default (vllm_ascend/platform.py:68) and most models carry no TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper submodules (only DeepSeek V4 MTP/dspark use @support_torch_compile), so PIECEWISE/FULL_AND_PIECEWISE will silently downgrade to NONE/FULL_DECODE_ONLY during MRV2 warmup even though ascend supports piecewise splitting (set_splitting_ops_for_v1 in platform.py:1196-1207, breakable_aclgraph.py). Patch/override the MRV2 graph-init path to pass piecewise_capture_available=True when ascend's ACL breakable-graph machinery is active, e.g. breakable_cudagraph.is_breakable_cudagraph_enabled() or when the custom compile backend yields compiled submodules.

2. New fallback value in VllmConfig.__post_init__: For non-VLLM_COMPILE configs, cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE now normalizes to FULL_DECODE_ONLY (was NONE) BEFORE ascend's check_and_update_config runs, so ascend no longer sees the previous eager path; it enters the has_full_cudagraphs() branch (platform.py:1214) and captures FULL_DECODE_ONLY decode ACL graphs instead of running fully eager. Validate this config combination on NPU (the ROCm-specific gfx950/DeepSeekV4 eager default added in this commit is CUDA/ROCm-only and does not apply to ascend).

3. The direct calls at vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py:5814 (MRV1) and vllm_ascend/_310p/worker/v2/model_runner.py:486 (310P) omit the new kwarg (default True), so their behavior is unchanged; add a regression note that upstream may start passing this kwarg. MRV1 also uses its own compile_or_warm_up_model (vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py:867), so it is unaffected by the model_runner.py change.

4. _validate_adaptive_verification now requires has_full_cudagraphs() instead of merely != NONE; no ascend action needed since vllm-ascend has no adaptive-verification implementation.
deep_analysis.risk: Low to medium. No compile-time/API breakage for OOT platforms. The real risk is silent behavioral change: (a) MRV2 piecewise graph users may lose piecewise splitting (perf regression) because piecewise_capture_available defaults to False on ascend; (b) configs that previously ran fully eager (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE + compilation disabled) now engage FULL_DECODE_ONLY ACL graph capture on NPU, which could surface graph-capture incompatibilities not exercised before. Both are easy to miss because they degrade gracefully rather than erroring, so end-to-end validation of piecewise/FULL_DECODE_ONLY modes on Ascend hardware is required.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This upstream commit rewrites the MRV2 PCPManager to natively support spec decode (single-module MTP and replicated DSpark) by removing its RequestState (req_states) dependency, repartitioning local batches from positions/seq_lens instead of request state, and adding a draft-prefill PCP path (get_draft_input_buffers/prepare_draft_prefill/restore_draft_prefill/restore_hidden_states). It also wires speculator.pcp_manager in GPUModelRunner, passes target_attn_layer_names to check_attention_cp_compatibility, and forces PCP=1 inside DFlashSpeculator.__init__. vllm-ascend has a bespoke replicated-PCP draft design that directly collides with these changes. Required adaptations:

1. HARD BREAK — AscendPCPManager.__init__ (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/pcp_manager.py:54-78): the subclass still declares req_states and forwards req_states=req_states to super().__init__(); upstream PCPManager.__init__ removed that parameter, so every PCP run (prefill_context_parallel_size>1) on Ascend will raise TypeError. Remove the req_states parameter, stop forwarding it, and drop the `from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.states import RequestState` import. This also applies to the manager construction path since NPUModelRunnerV2.pcp_manager_cls = AscendPCPManager and upstream maybe_build_pcp_manager no longer passes req_states.

2. partition_batch / _partition_speculative_batch_compat (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/pcp_manager.py:153-329): upstream rewrote partition_batch — it now gathers positions into the local input buffers and derives seq_lens from local end positions (local_query_start_loc[1:]-1), sets self._local_batch and self._local_gather_idx, and no longer uses prepare_pos_seq_lens/combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens (removed from the module) nor self._local_req_idx. The Ascend override must be reconciled with the new local-batch/seq_lens/positions semantics, and _partition_speculative_batch_compat must also refresh the upstream-stored self._local_batch (currently it only restores self._global_batch and returns a replaced AscendInputBatch), otherwise the new draft-prefill methods consume a stale/inconsistent _local_batch.

3. New upstream draft-prefill path will now execute on Ascend: NPUModelRunnerV2.initialize_kv_cache (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py:252) sets speculator.pcp_manager, and AscendAutoRegressiveSpeculator.propose/_run_model/_generate_draft/_prefill call super(), which after this commit invokes pcp_manager.prepare_draft_prefill/get_draft_input_buffers/restore_draft_prefill and block_tables.gather_block_tables. This overlaps vllm-ascend's replicated-PCP design (prepare_replicated_pcp_config sets draft PCP=1 and disable_target_pcp_for_replicated_draft detaches model_state.pcp_manager, but the upstream code reads speculator.pcp_manager, not model_state.pcp_manager). The upstream draft_prefill_batch/_local_batch are plain InputBatch/InputBuffers, not AscendInputBatch/AscendInputBuffers, so draft attention metadata and FIA tiling could receive the wrong layout, and hidden states may be restored twice. Decide between (a) adopting the upstream path and overriding the new PCPManager draft-prefill methods to build AscendInputBatch, or (b) neutralizing it for the replicated design (e.g. keep speculator.pcp_manager=None / gate the base hooks on replicated_pcp in pcp_utils.py).

4. DFlash/DSpark (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py, dspark/speculator.py): upstream DFlashSpeculator.__init__ now copies vllm_config and forces prefill_context_parallel_size=1, duplicating prepare_replicated_pcp_config in AscendDSparkSpeculator; and upstream propose() now gathers block tables when pcp_manager is not None. Verify no double config handling and that replicated_pcp detection remains correct.

5. MTP (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/mtp/speculator.py): AscendMTPSpeculator inherits MTPSpeculator whose share_mtp_topk_indices is now forced off when PCP>1; confirm DeepSeek-V4/GLM MTP + PCP behavior is unaffected on NPU.

6. model_runner execute_model (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py:263-296 calls super().execute_model): upstream now uses draft_hidden_states captured BEFORE PCP restore for speculator.propose and restores aux_hidden_states via pcp_manager.restore_hidden_states. Align _restore_replicated_draft_target_states/sample_tokens so the draft gets the PCP-local hidden states exactly once (no double restore) and sampling gets the global layout.

7. check_attention_cp_compatibility: the new target_layer_names argument is optional, so the vllm_ascend/_310p/worker/v2/model_runner.py:503 single-arg call still compiles; but review the semantic change (upstream now only enforces PCP backend support on target layers).

8. Tests — tests/ut/worker/test_pcp_manager_v2.py: remove req_states from AscendPCPManager(...) constructions (lines 130, 229, 540, 1017) and remove/replace patch('vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pcp_manager.prepare_pos_seq_lens') and patch('vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pcp_manager.combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens') (lines 245-249, 558-562) — those module attributes no longer exist after this commit.
deep_analysis.risk: High. (1) Hard runtime break: AscendPCPManager still forwards req_states to the upstream constructor, so any Ascend run with prefill_context_parallel_size>1 crashes with TypeError immediately after this commit lands. (2) Behavioral collision: the new upstream draft-prefill PCP path executes inside the inherited AutoRegressiveSpeculator/DFlashSpeculator code that vllm-ascend's speculators call via super(), conflicting with the bespoke replicated-PCP mechanism (plain vs AscendInputBatch layout, double hidden-state restore, block-table gather duplication), which can cause incorrect attention metadata / FIA tiling and wrong sampled tokens on NPU. (3) The rewritten partition_batch positions/seq_lens derivation changes the local-batch contract that AscendPCPManager.partition_batch and _partition_speculative_batch_compat depend on. (4) vllm-ascend's PCP unit tests will fail (removed module attributes, req_states kwarg). Sparse MLA/DCP indexer code (sparse_attn_indexer.py) is lower risk because vllm-ascend uses its own indexers (AscendIndexerOps/SparseAttnIndexerKpool) and does not import the upstream op.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: The upstream commit (vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py) stops zero-progress preemption cascades in the allocate_slots-retry loop by checking the new `_request_blocks_can_be_freed(request)` helper (inherited from Scheduler) before preempting a victim when `defer_block_free=True`. vllm-ascend's custom schedulers duplicate this loop verbatim and would retain the pre-fix cascade behavior, so they must be ported to match after rebase. For each of the four duplicated loops (recompute_scheduler.py:383-489, dyntra_lb_scheduler.py:562-612, patch_balance_schedule.py:303-345, scheduler_profiling_chunk.py:375-416): (1) select the victim WITHOUT removing it yet (peek `max(self.running, key=(priority, arrival_time))` for PRIORITY, or `self.running[-1]` for FCFS instead of an immediate `pop()`); (2) add `if not self._request_blocks_can_be_freed(preempted_req): break` before the `del/remove/pop` and before `_preempt_request()`, so the victim stays RUNNING and the current request is simply not scheduled this step (it retries once fences drain via `_drain_deferred_frees`); (3) keep the existing victim_index/req_index bookkeeping only on the actually-preempted path. Special care in RecomputeScheduler: its preemption branch can offload blocks to the connector (`connector.update_state_before_preempt`) which relocates KV remotely before the deferred local free, so verify the guard placement does not silently skip that offload path; if offload genuinely releases blocks it should still be allowed, otherwise mirror upstream semantics (fenced victim cannot satisfy the local allocation). Add regression tests in tests/ut/core/ mirroring upstream test_deferred_block_free.py::test_allocation_retry_waits_for_fence_then_succeeds (policy=fcfs/priority + failing allocate_slots) and test_async_scheduler.py::test_kv_pressure_preempt_mid_handoff (defer_free=True => victim stays RUNNING, no preemption). Schedulers that delegate to super().schedule() (ShortRequestFirstScheduler, BatchJobAwareScheduler) need no changes; the default Scheduler/AsyncScheduler path inherits the fix automatically.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. No interface/signature changes, so no compile/runtime breakage on the default path (SchedulerOutput, SchedulerInterface, KVCacheManager unchanged). Primary risk is behavioral divergence: if not ported, the custom schedulers keep the pre-fix cascade (mass preemption with zero allocation progress, potentially preempting the very request being scheduled) under deferred frees on PD KV-consumer/async deployments; if ported naively, the RecomputeScheduler's connector-offload preemption path may be skipped (the fenced-victim guard fires before the offload branch), changing PD KV hand-off semantics. Requires careful placement of the guard relative to the recompute-offload branch and regression tests on both PRIORITY and FCFS policies.

affected_interfaces: NPUModelRunner.prepare_inputs (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py:318) — the override bypasses the new upstream fast-prefill arming, so kv_sharing_fast_prefill is silently a no-op on Ascend V2

AscendModelState.prepare_attn (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_states/default.py:44) — doesn't thread input_batch.fast_prefill into Ascend's build_attn_metadata

NPUPlatform.check_and_update_config (vllm_ascend/platform.py) — upstream removed the V2 unsupported-feature guard for kv_sharing_fast_prefill, so it must be re-guarded for the V2 path or Ascend silently drops the optimization

AscendAttentionMetadataBuilder (vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py:212) — gets wrapped by upstream's create_fast_prefill_custom_backend('FastPrefill', ...) in init_attn_backend when the flag is on; needs to tolerate the wrapper and the reduced-metadata type
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: This commit enables MRV2 fast-prefill in upstream: it removes 'KV sharing fast prefill' from VllmConfig._get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features() (so V2 + kv_sharing_fast_prefill is no longer rejected), adds FastPrefillHelper/FastPrefillBatchMetadata and get_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_eligible_layers to vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py, adds a draft_layer_names kwarg to init_attn_backend and a fast_prefill kwarg to build_attn_metadata, adds InputBatch.fast_prefill, and makes make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata() degrade gracefully (return full metadata) instead of asserting when logits_indices_padded is None. On Ascend, NPUModelRunnerV2 inherits GPUModelRunner, so its initialize_kv_cache runs the new code (FastPrefillHelper created, Ascend attention backends wrapped with FastPrefillAttentionBuilder for eligible KV-sharing layers), but Ascend's own prepare_inputs never sets input_batch.fast_prefill and Ascend's own build_attn_metadata ignores it — so the feature becomes a silent no-op (correct results, no fast-prefill). No existing vllm-ascend code breaks (all new params are defaulted; AscendInputBatch picks up fast_prefill=None via fields(InputBatch); Ascend resets ubatch_size to 0). Minimal adaptation: in NPUPlatform.check_and_update_config, raise ValueError when vllm_config.cache_config.kv_sharing_fast_prefill and vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner (mirroring the removed upstream check) until Ascend V2 implements it — V1 runner (vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py) already supports it via _prepare_kv_sharing_fast_prefill. Optional full support on V2: (1) add a FastPrefillHelper and arm input_batch.fast_prefill in NPUModelRunner.prepare_inputs from cu_num_logits_np/batch_req_state.has_prefill/batch_desc; (2) add fast_prefill kwarg to vllm_ascend/worker/v2/attn_utils.py::build_attn_metadata and set logits_indices_padded/num_logits_indices/max_logits_per_req on AscendCommonAttentionMetadata; (3) pass input_batch.fast_prefill from AscendModelState.prepare_attn; (4) resolve the type mismatch where upstream make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata returns a plain CommonAttentionMetadata lacking Ascend fields (attn_state, query_start_loc_cpu pad, etc.) that Ascend builders require — e.g. override/customize the FastPrefill wrapper to keep the AscendCommonAttentionMetadata subtype; (5) note vllm_ascend/_310p/worker/v2/model_runner.py:469 calls init_attn_backend without the new draft_layer_names kwarg, so draft-layer exclusion for the eligible-layer walk is skipped there.
deep_analysis.risk: Low-to-moderate. No existing vllm-ascend functionality regresses: this only relaxes a previously-rejected config combination. Main risks are (a) silent performance regression — users enabling --kv-sharing-fast-prefill on Ascend V2 get no optimization and no warning since the wrapped FastPrefill builder gracefully falls back to full-batch execution (the commit's assert→graceful-return change is what prevents a crash here); (b) latent crash if Ascend ever arms fast_prefill naively, because the reduced metadata produced by upstream's make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata is a plain CommonAttentionMetadata that AscendMetadataBuilder (which requires Ascend-specific fields like attn_state) cannot consume; (c) on 310P V2 the direct init_attn_backend call omits draft_layer_names, so speculative-draft KV-sharing layers could be misclassified as fast-prefill-eligible when the flag is combined with spec decode.
